questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

The minister __promise to looked into__ the matter of fuel emissions and air pollution.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1.**
 
• The given sentence should be in the past tense i.e. 'promise' must be replaced by 'promised'. The infinitive verb follows the structure 'TO + V1' so replace 'to looked' with 'to look'.
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence is 'The minister **promised to look **into the matter of fuel emissions and air pollution.'

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

The team began searching for reasons for their poor performance in the tournament.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The correct answer is** Option 2).**
 
• The error lies in the wrong usage of the pronoun **'their' **and should be replaced by** 'Its' **because **team** is a **collective noun** and **all the members of the are working as one unit**__ so its will be treated as** a singular noun** and the pronoun to be used is** 'it'.**
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence is *'The team began searching for reasons for **its **poor performance in the tournament.'*

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. We had already covered half the distance when we reached a three-road junction.

B. I was worried it might pounce on us.

C. But thankfully we picked up speed and it got left behind.

D. Suddenly, a barking dog began to chase the bike for some distance.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• Sentence A is the only independent sentence among the given sentences, so A is the first sentence.
 
• Sentence A is talking about a journey which is continued by sentence D with an incident mentioning about dog chasing the bike.
 
• **This sequence of AD is given only in option 2 i.e. ADBC**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Using matches however came much later.

B. The first great discovery that man probably made was that of fire.

C. In olden times fires were made by rubbing two flints against each other till a spark was produced.

D. And this spark set fire to dry straw, leaves or wood.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 3.**
 
• Among the given sentences, there are two independent sentences i.e. B & C. But sentence B is introducing the subject i.e. 'fire' so B is the first sentence.
 
• Sentence C is talking about how the spark was produced which is continued by sentence D.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sequence BCDA is given in option 3.**

questions.question:

have will be changed into had.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

She was unable to produce sufficient evidences to support her accusations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. sufficient evidences to.**

__
 
• **Evidence** is an** uncountable noun.** Hence, we **cannot **make a **plural **of it by adding 's' at the end of it.

 To **make Plural**: **'pieces of'** will be added i.e '**pieces of evidence'**.
 
• So, the correct sentence __will be: *She was unable to produce sufficient __**evidence**__ to support her accusations.*
 
• Other uncountable nouns are: Furniture, information, luggage, jewellery, scenery, postage, percentage, etc.
